ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows an arrow-pushing mechanism diagram of a six-membered nitrogen-containing heterocycle. The nitrogen atom slightly to the upper right on the ring is connected to SO2Ph and remains a sulfonamide-substituted nitrogen; the ring carbon slightly to the upper left is connected to an EtO2C ester group; the chiral ring carbon at the lower left is connected to Ph; the chiral ring carbon at the lower right is connected to OEt and H. There are multiple curved arrows in the figure, indicating that the intraring π electrons move again along the six-membered ring from the original imine/enamine-type arrangement. Reasoning: After moving the electrons according to the arrows, the connection between N and SO2Ph is unchanged, and N still remains in the six-membered ring as a sulfonamide nitrogen; EtO2C is still connected to the upper-left ring carbon, and the configurations of the two chiral centers where Ph and OEt/H are located are retained. The electron rearrangement adjusts the intraring double bond to a C=C adjacent to the ester-group-substituted carbon, that is, forms a C1=C alkene bond, while N and this ester-group-substituted carbon are single-bond ring-closed. Therefore the six-membered N-heterocycle SMILES corresponding to the product is O=C(OCC)C1=C[C@@H](c2ccccc2)C[C@@H](OCC)N1S(=O)(c3ccccc3)=O.

method.method_draft: First describe the image structure and mark the atoms of the heterocycle. Follow the curved arrows one by one: move the indicated pi electrons around the cyclic system, convert the imine/enamine arrangement to the product alkene pattern, and leave the N bonded to SO2Ph as a sulfonamide. Keep the EtO2C group attached to the top-left ring carbon, keep the Ph substituent on the left chiral ring carbon, and keep the OEt/H substituent on the lower-right chiral ring carbon. After updating the bonds, draw the resulting six-membered N-heterocycle with the C=C bond adjacent to the ester-bearing carbon and with the two stereocenters retained. Convert this final structure to the SMILES string: O=C(OCC)C1=C[C@@H](c2ccccc2)C[C@@H](OCC)N1S(=O)(c3ccccc3)=O.
